extracted.intended_audience: corporate communications professionals, PR/social-media managers, brand and crisis managers, marketing agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Practical steps and principles for a corporation to detect, contain, and respond to a viral employee-misconduct video to protect brand reputation. Covers preparedness, identification and discipline of perpetrators, legal/removal actions, selective public engagement, owned-content counterprogramming, and outcome measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparedness infrastructure and crisis-readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Have established systems for recalls, suppliers, distribution, and crisis response so the organization can react when trust is threatened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes Domino’s had a "well oiled machine" for recalls and other crises (food distribution, suppliers, recall mechanisms). Guidance: maintain documented procedures, supplier controls, and response teams so operational issues can be handled while communications focus on reputation. Anti-pattern: relying on ad-hoc processes or only operational readiness without communications planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid detection and monitoring of online channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor online media and communities so incidents are discovered quickly (Domino’s learned of the video within an hour after Consumerist notified them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring of YouTube, blogs, forums, and Twitter; maintain contacts at watchdog sites. Scoring note: faster detection reduces time for false narratives to spread. Anti-pattern: discovering incidents only after mainstream pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying and taking action against the culprits
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture imagery from the content, crowdsource identification across locations, confirm identities, notify the franchise/store owner, and take personnel action (e.g., firing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps Domino’s used: capture digital stills, distribute message to all US locations to identify individuals, confirm identity and location, contact storeowner and request termination. Also consider documenting evidence for internal and external use. Anti-pattern: delaying or failing to identify responsible parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate to appropriate legal and public-health authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: When employee misconduct may implicate health or criminal concerns, contact Health Department and local police to file charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s contacted the Health Department and police because food contamination was alleged. Guidance: engage authorities promptly to demonstrate seriousness and to enable formal investigation. Anti-pattern: treating potential criminal/health issues as purely HR matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage platform policies and copyright to remove offending content
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with hosting platforms to remove content by asserting applicable policy or rights (e.g., copyright) and securing authorization from the uploader/copyright owner if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s social media team contacted YouTube; YouTube would remove the video only at copyright owner’s request. Company identified the filmer, secured a signed authorization letter from her (with her lawyer’s involvement), and used that to get the video pulled. Guidance: understand platform takedown rules, prepare documentation and legal authorization. Anti-pattern: assuming platforms will remove content on request without following platform procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectively delay mass public statements to avoid amplifying content
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid an immediate press release or news conference if doing so would draw more attention to the offending content; instead, respond selectively to inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s chose not to go public immediately, reasoning that public statements would drive more people to seek the original video. Guidance: evaluate when a broad announcement will amplify versus when containment and targeted outreach are preferable. Anti-pattern: reflexive broad press release that seeds curiosity and drives views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive engagement with sites/forums hosting discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate directly with forums and sites that posted or are discussing the content to correct narrative and provide the company perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s reached out to forums and sites hosting the video or conversations, stressing that the misconduct was done to the company (not by corporate policy). Guidance: provide factual context, request corrections or removals where appropriate, and supply official statements or evidence. Anti-pattern: ignoring or only responding via press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use owned channels (website and social) to centralize accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: Post an official statement on the company website and use social accounts to direct conversations and traffic to that authoritative source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s posted a statement on its website and used Twitter to direct users to it. Guidance: maintain a clear, accessible hub for company responses and link to it in replies/posts. Scoring note: clarity and accessibility of the hub improve message control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-program with authentic, senior-led owned content ("fighting fire with fire")
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce and publish an authentic company response (e.g., unscripted video from a senior leader) that acknowledges the issue, expresses appropriate emotion, and shows steps being taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s posted a flip-camera video of company president Patrick Doyle speaking calmly and sincerely. Guidance: authenticity and visible leadership can shift tone; unscripted can be effective. Anti-pattern: overly corporate, scripted, or defensive messaging that fails to convey sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use search and metadata strategy to ensure owned content outranks offending content
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply SEO/keyword tactics (e.g., mirror search terms used by original) so company content appears ahead in search results for key queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s used the word "disgusting" in their video title—the same word used in the original—so their video would surface first in searches. Guidance: craft titles, descriptions, and tags to capture search intent; expect that a response will increase overall visibility but can reframe results. Anti-pattern: posting content with irrelevant metadata that fails to surface for searching users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplify company response through social sharing and cross-posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the company’s response by posting links on Twitter, Facebook, and other channels to increase visibility of the official narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s posted links on Twitter and Facebook after uploading their video. Guidance: coordinate cross-channel promotion to direct audiences to the authoritative message; monitor reactions and engage where appropriate. Anti-pattern: relying on a single channel or neglecting follow-up engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and accept short-term amplification for long-term narrative control
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that a company response may temporarily increase views and attention but can change the story to focus on the company’s actions rather than the wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Domino’s posted their video, views of the original surged but the narrative morphed from "look at these disgusting people at Domino's" to "what is Domino's doing about it?" Guidance: weigh trade-offs—a timely response may raise short-term exposure but can reposition coverage. Scoring note: success measured by narrative shift and public perception trends, not only by reduced views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure outcomes and track impacts on business and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor metrics such as video views, search queries, media impressions, sales impacts, stock price, and customer-satisfaction indices to assess effects and recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s tracked video views (millions), search query volumes, estimated 60 million media impressions, sales effects among franchisees, stock stability, and ACSI placement. Guidance: use both quantitative (media impressions, sales) and qualitative (narrative change) measures. Anti-pattern: assuming no business impact without measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document lessons learned and advise/assist others
rubrics_metrics.description: After resolution, share learnings internally and externally to help other organizations prepare for similar incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s was later contacted by other organizations seeking advice. Guidance: convert experience into training, playbooks, and external thought-leadership. Scoring note: institutionalizing lessons improves future preparedness.
